variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Serverless MLOps uses short-lived, automatically scaled compute to react to ML events: a new dataset arrives, a schedule fires, an inference request appears, or a monitoring rule requests evaluation. The function usually validates and coordinates work; durable managed services store data, run long jobs, register artifacts, and serve models.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Receive a versioned event
pairs.detail: Carry a stable event ID, producer, schema version, dataset or model version, timestamp, and trace context.
pairs.explanation: Carry a stable event ID, producer, schema version, dataset or model version, timestamp, and trace context.

pairs.label: Validate and claim
pairs.detail: Authenticate the producer, validate the payload, enforce policy, and atomically map the event ID to one workflow ID.
pairs.explanation: Authenticate the producer, validate the payload, enforce policy, and atomically map the event ID to one workflow ID.

pairs.label: Launch durable work
pairs.detail: Submit data preparation, training, evaluation, or inference to compute whose lifetime and resources fit the job.
pairs.explanation: Submit data preparation, training, evaluation, or inference to compute whose lifetime and resources fit the job.

pairs.label: Record evidence
pairs.detail: Bind inputs, code, configuration, artifacts, metrics, approvals, and terminal state to the workflow identity.
pairs.explanation: Bind inputs, code, configuration, artifacts, metrics, approvals, and terminal state to the workflow identity.

pairs.label: Promote or quarantine
pairs.detail: Deploy only through an evidence gate; route poison events and failed jobs to an owned recovery path.
pairs.explanation: Deploy only through an evidence gate; route poison events and failed jobs to an owned recovery path.

The function usually validates and coordinates work; durable managed services store data, run long jobs, register artifacts, and serve models.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Synchronous function
pairs.detail: Use for small artifacts and bounded preprocessing when both warm and cold paths meet the deadline.
pairs.explanation: Use for small artifacts and bounded preprocessing when both warm and cold paths meet the deadline. Protect downstreams from automatic concurrency.

pairs.label: Queue-backed worker
pairs.detail: Use when completion can be asynchronous.
pairs.explanation: Use when completion can be asynchronous. Queue age, attempt count, idempotency, dead letters, and result identity become part of the contract.

pairs.label: Durable training job
pairs.detail: Let the function submit a managed job with explicit input, image, resource, checkpoint, timeout, and output locations.
pairs.explanation: Let the function submit a managed job with explicit input, image, resource, checkpoint, timeout, and output locations. Do not train inside the trigger.

pairs.label: Dedicated endpoint
pairs.detail: Prefer an autoscaled serving fleet when utilization is continuous, artifacts are large, accelerators are required, or cold starts cannot meet the SLO.
pairs.explanation: Prefer an autoscaled serving fleet when utilization is continuous, artifacts are large, accelerators are required, or cold starts cannot meet the SLO.
